resources.string: The old-TV “electron beam” screen-off from Android 2.3 / 4.x, frame-accurate, on modern Android.
Plays the CRT animation and switches the screen off

Draws the CRT animation above everything, takes a snapshot of the screen for the animation (Android 11+, never saved), and switches the screen off like the power button, so fingerprint and face unlock keep working. It does not read anything on your screen and has no internet access.
Needed to draw the animation over everything and switch the screen off.

In Accessibility settings, open “Installed apps” (or “Downloaded apps”) → “CRT Off – screen-off service” and switch it on.

It only draws the animation, takes a snapshot of the screen for it, and switches the screen off. It does not read your screen content, and the app has no internet access.

If Android says it’s a restricted setting: App info → ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Android 13+: if the switch is greyed out, open App info → ⋮ menu → “Allow restricted settings” first. Xiaomi / Oppo / Vivo: also set battery to “No restrictions”.
Turn on the CRT Off screen-off service first
Plays over this screen without switching the screen off. Real speed is 350 ms: warm-up with a mirrored ghost (67 ms), collapse to a white line (150 ms), then the line shrinks and fades (133 ms).
Tap it to switch off with the CRT animation. Drag it to move; it snaps to the screen edge. At 0 % it is invisible but still works where you left it.
For phones with a camera button, like Sony Xperia. A single press still works as the camera shutter; holding it still opens the camera.
Press Volume Down twice quickly to switch off. The first press still changes the volume by one step.
Pull down Quick Settings, tap the pencil/edit button and drag “CRT off” into your tiles.
Your launcher doesn’t support adding shortcuts. Long-press the app icon instead.
Samsung: Settings → Advanced features → Side key → Double press → Open app → “CRT off now”. Double-pressing the side key then plays the CRT off.
Plays your lock click as the screen goes dark, only when the ringer is on. If you hear two clicks, turn off Android’s own “Screen lock sound”.

• Android doesn’t let apps animate the real power button: apps are only told after the screen is already dark. Use the floating button, the tile, the shortcut or Volume Down instead.
• Turning the screen on is instant, exactly as in the original Android 2.3 / 4.x.
• Android 11+: the real picture on your screen collapses. Android 9–10 can’t take snapshots, so black shutters close in around the screen in the same shape.
• Banking and other protected screens block snapshots; they use the shutter version too.
• Your PIN, pattern, fingerprint and face unlock all keep working.
• No internet permission.
